propositions: Commit subjects exceeding 50 characters are rejected at commit time with output naming the offending line and its length.
Commit body lines exceeding 72 characters are rejected at commit time with output naming each offending line and its length.
Conforming commits pass the 50/72 check and still receive Gerrit's Change-Id trailer via the chained commit-msg.legacy hook, not clobbered by pre-commit install.

Carve-outs from the 72-column rule include trailers, TAG= lines, fenced code blocks, 4+ space/tab-indented blocks, table rows, and lines where over-length is due solely to unsplittable tokens (URLs, paths, dotted identifiers).
The check-only implementation never mutates the commit message and correctly ignores git scaffolding (comment lines and --verbose diff).

pre-commit install -f must not be run to preserve Gerrit's hook; make hooks verifies both hook types and the Change-Id chain, exiting non-zero if either hook is absent and warning (but exiting zero) if Change-Id stamping is not found.
